verifications.evidence: All three reproductions executed in tmp trees (scratchpad/r2-257/repro.ts): symlinked skills root, symlinked category, symlinked skill dir. In every case the victim SKILL.zed.md survives, the sweep returns exactly one skipped-dir outcome with reason "symlink", and the warning names the blocked component. Category probed once, so one symlinked category yields one notice rather than 67.

The tmp filesystem here is case-insensitive — existsSync("SKILL.zed.md") returns true for an on-disk skill.zed.md. With that file present the sweep returns an empty list and the file survives; readdir plus exact-name matching is what does the work.

Happy path removes a genuine stale build and returns {action:"removed"}, rendered as a printed notice. SKILL.md, SKILL.detail.md and reference.md are untouched; a symlink as the candidate file gives kept-not-regular-file with the target intact.

The message at src/gdskills/bundled-eval.ts:1986 now says "Split the skill... A ceiling only ever moves DOWN"; the Length Ceilings blockquote in skills-storage-workflow.mdc matches it word for word, compared by hand. bundled-eval.test.ts:1704-1718 reads both files. The .metaproject mirror is byte-identical to the bundled copy.

RANK1_FIRST=285 and RANK1_TOTAL=287 are both re-measured live and compared with toBe, not a bound; the denominator is the corpus's own counted positives. Lowering silently is impossible — the only escape is KNOWN_ROUTING_GAPS[].excluded, a visible registry rather than a number. bun test src/commands/routing-corpus.test.ts: 181 pass, 0 fail.

Three tests at bundled-eval.test.ts:2035-2077 pin the ledger's existence, header, separator row, the append-only statement and the rule's citation; bun test src/gdskills/bundled-eval.test.ts gives 60 pass, 0 fail. The instructed CHECKED_PATH_ROOTS change was independently re-measured: package.json files does not publish docs/skills/, so the refusal holds; the replacement is sufficient for AC11.

Fixtures reject "not formatted", "not forced" and "not fortunate"; the control with a real NOT-for clause passes. skills verify --bundled passes every check across all 67 shipped skills, so the boundary introduces no false positive.
The determiner gate has its own unit test, and the sweep over the 67 shipped skills reports no description finding — the nouns that previously tripped it now pass.
A fixture skill carrying a Codex build produces exactly one anatomy:sections finding, not one per build.
A fixture with an empty Verification body is rejected; the control with a body passes.
A fixture whose Red Flags rows are placeholders is rejected; the shipped tree passes, so the floor does not fire on real tables.
anatomy:red-flags-collision exists, fires on a fixture pair sharing a table, is attributed to the later key only, and reports nothing on the shipped tree.
Both interview and interviewer are present in the catalog, so the rewritten NOT-for clause resolves to a skill that exists.
The quoted row in reviewer-skill-creator matches src/review/reviewers.ts:200-205 exactly, including the "no recorded origin" case for drift === "none".
keryx flow check was run: it takes no flow id, so the argument the skill used to pass was wrong and its removal is correct.

The storage rule now enumerates both divergence cases — different instructions, different metadata.compatible_harnesses — and names the seven gproject skills that qualify; 15 runtime builds remain in the tree, consistent with that list.
